turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on? Patient: I had an open cholecystectomy, and about three days later I developed fever and chills with a headache. I also started having a productive cough for the last 12 hours and right-sided chest pain that gets worse when I take a deep breath.

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your symptoms, have you experienced any changes in your vision, such as blurriness, blind spots, or any loss of sight?
turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t noticed any changes in my vision like blurriness, blind spots, or any loss of sight. Mostly it’s the fever and chills with my productive cough and the right-sided chest pain that’s worse with deep breaths.

turns.doctor_question: To help me get a better picture of your overall health, could you tell me if you currently smoke or have a history of smoking?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, I have a history of smoking—about one pack of cigarettes a day for roughly 17 years. I’m not having any vision changes, but the fever and productive cough with the right-sided chest pain still persist.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of how you're feeling, have you been experiencing any nausea or feeling sick to your stomach?
turns.patient_answer: “I’ve had some general discomfort and feeling sick since the surgery, but I haven’t had any significant nausea or vomiting. It’s mainly the fever and chills, the productive cough, and the sharp right-sided chest pain when I take a deep breath.”
